ground_truth.main_content:
Tips from a first time Japan visitor

Dec 31, 2025, 9:37 PM

Japan tips from a first time visitor

As our trip is drawing to a close I thought Ive give tips from a first time visitor -

I did lots and lots of research before visiting Japan and thank the feedback and info from this forum. We also talked to friends who had been to Japan. This really helped us to be prepared.

We visited Japan in late December and early January. Despite being a really busy time we never felt crowded, busy or rushed.

Plan and stay in a good location - it will save you lots of time with travel. We still spent lots of time getting to and from and waiting at train stations and pedestrian crossings!

Learn some Japanese phases - at a minimum learn hello, thank you, excuse me, before meal thanks, after meal thanks, thank you. And use them often. And a respectful nod! The locals really appreciated our attempts and use of Japanese greetings and phases.

Follow signs and google maps to get to the right train station entry/exit, the correct line, train platform and platform number and train. If you get these steps right its easy to use the trains. For example on the Nozomi shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo we got the taxi driver to drop us off at the hachijo south shinkansen entry, saves navigating the station, we then looked for the Tokaido shrinkansen platform and just followed the signs. we were in the station about 3 minutes total.

Planning each of the steps right makes it so much easier. For local trains find the correct station entry, find the line and colour and then follow the signs to the platform you need. Book your tickets - they are easy to change online. We changed our shinkansen tickets online to an earlier train. Took about a minute and we had the peace of mind that we did have tickets secured and didnt have to wait in lines.

Be respectful - dont smoke and walk, dont eat and walk, dont talk on trains, keep mobile phones on silent (in fact i kept my phone on silent the whole time i was in Japan). No talking on mobile phones on public trains - and we noticed this extended to walking as well.

Reserve your seats on Nagano snow monkey express train. For $2 you are guaranteed a comfortable seat. The unreserved cars were crowded and standing room only. I think it was the best 300yen i spent. Get the seats at the front of the yukemuri train from yudanaka to nagano. for the front amazing window views we were on yukemuri snow monkey express carriage 4, seats 12A, B, C, D from yudanaka to nagano - the first service of the day. I purchased the tickets as soon as they were available online and the wrap around front glass and side window views are absolutely incredible. Best train ride I have ever done.

I brought some NZ souvenir pins with me and gave them to people who were kind and helped us - they appreciated it.

Google translate is not always reliable. One menu we translated said we were eating a stolen car!

Enjoy the food. Experience at least one Japanese ryoken. Do a japanese cooking class. Do a tea ceremony.

Wear good walking shoes and explore. We walked lots - 30,000 steps a day was usual for us (but we walk alot at home so thats not uncommon either). Get to busy places early and avoid crowds. Book things you want to do as they book out. Plan your day to get most effective use of time, but dont overplan.

Our itinerary was one night in Narita, 6 nights Shinjuku, Tokyo (with day trip to mt Fuji and lakes area), 2 nights Shibu Onsen (and snow monkeys in the snow), 5 nights Kyoto (with day trip to Osaka), 1 night Tokyo station, Tokyo. We felt this was a really good first time itinerary. If we werent travelling at New Year we would have changed kyoto to 4 nights and had final two nights elsewhere, but we were mindful that it was public holidays anf busiest travel days. Our favourite place was Shibu Onsen, our least liked place was Osaka.

I really recommend checking weather forecasts when you arrive before arranging trip to see Mt Fuji. We had one day with a sunny, clear, calm forecast. So we went to Mt Fuji on this day. It was absolutely perfect. Beautiful reflections of Mt Fuji in the lake, amazing views with not a cloud in the sky. If you can, check weather forecast and then choose the best day. Go early before the crowds. We left tokyo at 6am and had no crowds. When we left afternoon clouds were starting to form.

Enjoy the food - we ate lots of wonderful foods, some foods we still dont know what we were eating. And 7/11 really does have the best egg sandwiches!

We used the luggage forwarding on one occasion (at busy times overnight is not guaranteed) - the rest of the time we found it easy to travel on the trains with our luggage - and our experience is that many many people travel local, express and shinkansen trains with luggage and no issues. you just have to be able to lift and store, or may have to carry up stairs - and less than 160cm dimensions.

Our favourite place was Shibu Onsen. A charming quaint village with 9 public onsens. We loved everything about Shibu Onsen and our 2 nights there was wonderful. Kyoto was also a delight, and Osaka was our least liked place. There is so much to do in Tokyo so plan your time, but dont overplan!
